A. Left children are smaller, right children are larger
B. All nodes at each level are sorted
C. The tree is always perfectly balanced
D. Child values are the average of their parent and sibling

**A.** In a BST, every node must have smaller values in its left subtree and larger values in its right subtree.

**Pattern**: structural equality check

**Why**: Two trees are the same if their roots have equal values and both subtrees are identical. Recursion naturally expresses this.

**Python**: `recursion; compare node values and recurse on subtrees`

Front: LeetCode 104: Maximum Depth of Binary Tree
Back:
**Pattern**: post-order traversal

**Why**: Depth of a tree is one plus the maximum depth of its subtrees. Recursion unwraps this definition.

**Python**: `recursion; max(depth(left), depth(right)) + 1`

**Pattern**: constrained recursion

**Why**: A BST must satisfy bounds at every node. Recursion tracks constraints: left subtree < node < right subtree.

**Python**: `recursion; pass min and max bounds down the tree`

Front: LeetCode 102: Binary Tree Level Order Traversal
Back:

**Pattern**: postorder traversal tracking global max

**Why**: The diameter passes through some node as the longest path from left to right. Recursion computes heights and tracks the max sum.

**Python**: `recursion; track height and update max diameter`

Front: Prove: Dynamic array append is amortized O(1)
Back:
A sequence of n appends to a geometrically growing array costs O(n) time in total.

Complexity: O(n) for n appends; O(1) amortized, O(n) worst case for a single resize.

Front: Invariant: Dynamic array append is amortized O(1)
Back: After every append, capacity is at least length; immediately after a resize, capacity is at most twice length.
The first append writes one slot into the initial capacity and performs no copy.

Front: Proof step: Resize points form a geometric series
Back:
Capacity doubles only when length reaches capacity, so resizes happen at lengths 1, 2, 4, 8, and so on.

Depends on: base

Front: Proof step: Total copy work is bounded
Back:
Across all resizes the array copies at most 1 + 2 + 4 + ... + n slots, which is less than 2n.

Depends on: doubling

Front: Proof step: Add writes and copies
Back:
n appends perform n writes and fewer than 2n copies, so the sequence is linear and each append is O(1) on average.

Depends on: copies

Constructing a binary heap by calling sift-down from the last internal node to the root takes O(n) time.

Complexity: O(n) time and O(1) extra space, versus O(n log n) for repeated insertion.
Before node i is processed, every subtree rooted at an index greater than i is already a valid heap.
Nodes with no children already satisfy the heap property, so processing can start at the last parent.

Front: Proof step: Process internal nodes bottom-up
Back:
Walking from the last parent down to the root guarantees each child subtree is a heap before its parent is fixed.

Depends on: leaves

Front: Proof step: Cost depends on height
Back:
A node at height h moves at most h levels, and a binary heap has at most ceil(n / 2^(h+1)) nodes at height h.

Depends on: reverse

Front: Proof step: Bound the weighted sum
Back:
The sum over heights of h * n / 2^(h+1) is at most n, because the series sum h / 2^h converges to 2.

Depends on: height-cost

Front: Prove: Sliding window moves each pointer at most n times
Back:
A sliding window over an array of n elements runs in O(n) time when each pointer only moves forward.

Complexity: O(n) time, O(1) extra space.

Front: Invariant: Sliding window moves each pointer at most n times
Back: At the start of every iteration the half-open interval [left, right) is the current window and right is one past the last inspected element.
Set left = right = 0. The window is empty and the invariant holds before any input is consumed.

Front: Proof step: Right pointer only advances
Back:
Each iteration admits at most one new element by increasing right, so right advances at most n times.

Depends on: init

Front: Proof step: Left pointer only advances
Back:
Invalid windows are repaired by increasing left; it never decreases, so left also advances at most n times.

Depends on: init

Front: Proof step: Sum the pointer moves
Back:
At most n expansions plus at most n shrink steps gives O(n) total work, with O(1) extra space.

Depends on: expand, shrink
